subject: Renewal: Transition plan and updated monthly commit for 8→16 GPU reserved pool
messages:
From: Alex Green <alex.green@saasco.com>
To: priyom_das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal conversation — reserved pool increase question

Hi Priyom,

Our renewal is coming up in June and the product team is pushing to move from our current 8-GPU reserved pool to 16 GPUs to support a new generative feature. Can you outline what the updated monthly commit would look like and any options for a phased increase (e.g., start with 12 for 30 days then 16)? Also need to understand how throughput guarantees change — we currently have a soft target of 2K tokens/sec sustained.

We’ll need this for the procurement calendar as we evaluate the budget.

Thanks,
Alex Green
Head of AI Platform, SaaSCo
From: priyom_das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Green <alex.green@saasco.com>
Cc: rafael_mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>, monica_patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 10:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal conversation — reserved pool increase question

Alex — thanks for the heads up. High-level response below; attaching a formal proposal and a short migration runbook.

Key points:
- Proposed monthly commit: $52,500/mo (16 x V100-equivalent reserved GPUs). This reflects a 12-month renewal term and a 10% volume credit compared to on-demand.
- Phased ramp: we can do a 30-day 12-GPU canary with prorated pricing, then shift to 16 GPUs for remainder of term. No additional provisioning fee for the ramp.
- Throughput guarantee: we can commit to 95th percentile sustained throughput of 3,800 tokens/sec for the 16-GPU pool (per your current model mix). For the 12-GPU canary we publish an expected 2,800 tokens/sec. SLAs include a credit schedule tied to monthly availability/throughput percentiles.

Next steps I propose:
1) I’ll send the formal amendable proposal for procurement (attached).
2) Rafael (SE) can run a short sizing run against your mixed workload to validate latencies and token throughput.
3) If procurement is comfortable, sign the amendment and we schedule a 2-week migration window during the renewal effective date.

Attachments: ReservedPool_8to16_Proposal_v3.pdf; migration_runbook.md; throughput_sla_table.csv

—Priyom
Priyom Das
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: rafael_mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Green <alex.green@saasco.com>, priyom_das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: monica_patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 23 Apr 2027 08:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal conversation — reserved pool increase question

Alex — quick technical note:
- The 3,800 tokens/sec 95p is achievable assuming your average prompt length remains in the 300–400 token range and KV/cache hit rates stay > 60%. If you plan on longer context or heavier tool-calling we should re-run the load test.
- Network egress and batch sizing will affect sustained throughput; we recommend pinning model variants and enabling prefix KV caching to hit the numbers.
- For the 12→16 canary approach: we’ll provision both pools in parallel but route 20% of production traffic to the new pool during the canary so we can observe tail latency before full cutover.

I can run the sizing test next Tuesday if that works for you.

—Rafael
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Procurement Team <procurement@saasco.com>
To: priyom_das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>, Alex Green <alex.green@saasco.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Apr 2027 11:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal conversation — reserved pool increase question

Folks,

Procurement needs two things before we can move: a one-page amendment summary showing the new monthly commitment and effective date, and confirmation on termination terms/early-exit credits. Can you also confirm whether the 12-month term is standard or if there are options for a 24-month commit with deeper discounts?

Thanks,
Jen Park (on behalf of SaaSCo Procurement)
procurement@saasco.com
From: priyom_das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>
To: Procurement Team <procurement@saasco.com>, Alex Green <alex.green@saasco.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, rafael_mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 03 May 2027 09:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal conversation — reserved pool increase question

Jen — appreciate the clarity. Answers inline: 
- One-page amendment: attached (ReservedPool_8to16_Proposal_v3.pdf) — includes the monthly commit of $52,500, effective on the renewal date June 1, 2027.
- Term options: 12-month is baseline. We can offer a 24-month with an additional 8% discount to the monthly commit and a 60-day notice early-exit schedule with scaled credits.
- Early-exit: for 12-month terms we offer standard prorated credits based on remaining months; for 24-month the credit curve is more favorable (detailed table in throughput_sla_table.csv).

Internal note to Laura: Approving a 24-month 8% discount would reduce ARR velocity but improves unit economics and stickiness. Would you prefer we push for the 24-month with discount or keep the 12-month?

—Priyom
From: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: priyom_das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>, Alex Green <alex.green@saasco.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@saasco.com>
Date: Sat, 15 May 2027 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal conversation — reserved pool increase question

Thanks team — happy to move forward on the following agreed items to close the renewal: 
- Term: 24-month commitment at $48,300/mo (8% discount applied) with a June 1, 2027 effective date.
- Phased ramp: 30-day 12-GPU canary (20% traffic) then full 16-GPU cutover.
- Throughput SLA: 95p sustained 3,800 tokens/sec with monthly reporting; credits tiered by percent shortfall.
- Migration: Redwood to own provisioning and final cutover; SaaSCo to provide access to a masked sample workload and a test endpoint.

Alex/Jen — expect a formal amendment in your inbox by EOD Monday and a DocuSign link to follow. Rafael — please schedule the sizing run next Tuesday per earlier note.

Laura Bennett
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
